title: Too Slow? Vertical Circle Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A roller coaster loops the loop, a toy car loops its track, and a bucket of water swings over your head. All three go upside down at the top, so why does nothing fall? And why does Aarav get wet when he swings his bucket too slowly? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn motion in a vertical circle, for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, with JEE Main and NEET practice.

A live ball on a one metre string is started at the bottom. At 5 m/s the tension hits zero just past the side and the string goes slack. At 7 m/s it just makes it over the top, while a live graph of tension against angle shows the pull is biggest at the bottom (29.4 N) and zero at the top. We derive the slowest top speed, v = root(gr), and the bottom speed root(5gr) from energy, step by step. Side-by-side cards compare the bottom and the top, two pause-and-think questions test a weak rope and a stiff rod, and the bucket of water is explained link by link. Then a worked example, the exam trap about the top equation, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

In this video:
